title: Multi-Concept Quantitative Problems
tagline: Year 4 — Single problems that need two or three topics in sequence: profit with ratios, mixtures with percentages, work with wages

introduction.overview: A multi-concept problem cannot be solved with one formula; the answer of one step feeds the next. The usual pairs are profit with discount, ratio with percentage, work with wages, interest with ratio, and speed with ratio. The key is to write the chain of quantities (cost, marked price, selling price, profit) and compute each link in order.
introduction.placementRelevance: The harder questions in company papers are almost always of this type.
introduction.realWorldContext: Budgeting, pricing and project costing chain several calculations in the same way.

learningObjectives: Break a problem into a chain of single-topic steps
Handle profit, discount and marked price together
Split wages in proportion to work
Verify the final answer against an earlier step

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Marked price = cost × (1 + mark-up). Selling price = marked price × (1 − discount). Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

coreDefinitions: Chain: ordered quantities where each is computed from the previous one.
Mark-up: percentage added to cost to get the marked price.
Discount: percentage taken off the marked price.
Proportional wages: wages split in the ratio of work done.
Cross-check: recomputing from a different route.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: List the quantities in the order they depend on each other, and compute them as a chain.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write "cost → marked → selling → profit" (or the chain for the problem), fill known numbers, and compute one link at a time.

mainNarrative: A shopkeeper marks goods 25% above cost of ₹800, so the marked price is ₹1,000. After a 10% discount the selling price is ₹900 and the profit is ₹100, which is 12.5% of the cost.
Two workers A and B do 3 : 2 of a job; the wages of ₹5,000 are split in the same ratio: ₹3,000 and ₹2,000.
To mix 3 kg of tea at ₹40 with 5 kg at ₹60, the total cost is 120 + 300 = ₹420 for 8 kg, so ₹52.5 per kg.
If a salary is split in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 and the smallest share is ₹4,000, the total is ₹24,000 and the largest share ₹12,000.
Always check: the final selling price must exceed the cost if there is a profit.

deepDiveAspects.title: Chains hide base changes
deepDiveAspects.content: A discount applies to the marked price, not the cost; a profit is on the cost, not the selling price.

deepDiveAspects.title: Combine, then simplify
deepDiveAspects.content: Multiply the factors first (1.25 × 0.9 = 1.125) and apply once.

solvedExamples.title: Chain
solvedExamples.question: Goods cost ₹800, are marked 25% above cost and sold at 10% discount. Find the profit percentage.

solvedExamples.title: Wages
solvedExamples.question: A and B do 3 : 2 of a job and earn ₹5,000 together. What does A get?

solvedExamples.title: Mixture price
solvedExamples.question: 3 kg tea at ₹40 and 5 kg at ₹60 are mixed. Find the price per kg.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Do it all in the head.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write the chain of quantities and compute one link at a time; combine factors only at the end.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The selling price must be between cost and marked price when there is a discount.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Longer chains are just repeated single steps.

advanced.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a 10% discount and still gains 8%. His mark-up over cost (percent) is
advanced.explanation: Marked = cost × 1.08/0.9 = 1.2 × cost, so the mark-up is 20%.

A tank is filled by a pipe in 6 hours. After 2 hours a second pipe that fills it in 12 hours is also opened. The total time to fill is (hours)
placementStyle.explanation: In 2 h: 1/3 filled. Remaining 2/3 at 1/4 per hour: 8/3 h; total 2 + 8/3 = 4.67.

placementStyle.question: The average of 10 numbers is 40. When one number is replaced by 90 the average becomes 42. The replaced number was
placementStyle.explanation: Total rises by 20, so the old number was 90 − 20 = 70.
